B2a-08-rhizopus-mould-structure

Rhizopus growing on a slice of bread. Left: a slice of bread with patches of white fluffy mould and black dots. Right: an enlarged drawing of the mould: horizontal stolons arching over the bread surface; at each point where a stolon touches the bread, a cluster of branched rhizoids going down into the bread and a group of upright sporangiophores going up, each ending in a round black sporangium full of spores; one sporangium bursting to release spores. Show small arrows from the rhizoid tips into the bread labelled as enzymes, and arrows back into the rhizoids labelled as soluble food absorbed.
B2b-09-starch-test-leaf-steps

Step-by-step diagram of the iodine test for starch in a leaf, in six numbered panels in two rows. 1: a leaf in a beaker of boiling water over a Bunsen flame. 2: the flame turned off. 3: the leaf in a boiling tube of ethanol standing in the beaker of hot water (water bath), the ethanol turning green. 4: the now pale leaf being dipped in a beaker of warm water. 5: the leaf spread flat on a white tile. 6: iodine solution being added with a dropper, the leaf turning blue-black.
B3a-05-mammalian-heart-internal-section

Longitudinal (vertical) section of the mammalian heart in front view (so the right side of the heart is on the viewer's left). Show the four chambers with the thin-walled atria at the top and thick-walled ventricles below, the left ventricle wall clearly thickest, the septum, the tricuspid and bicuspid valves with chordae tendineae and papillary muscles, semilunar valves at the base of the pulmonary artery and aorta, and the major vessels. Blood on the right side tinted blue and on the left side tinted red, with small arrows showing flow.
B4a-04-tadpole-external-internal-gills

Two stages of a tadpole in side view. Left: a young tadpole with three pairs of feathery external gills (bright red) sticking out on each side behind the head. Right: an older tadpole with the gills covered by skin, and a small opening (the spiracle) on the left side, with arrows showing water entering the mouth and leaving through the spiracle.
B5-08-nephron-structure-detailed

Detailed diagram of a single nephron with its blood supply, arranged vertically with a dashed line marking the boundary between cortex (top) and medulla (bottom). Show the cup-shaped Bowman's capsule enclosing a red glomerulus; a wide afferent arteriole entering and a narrower efferent arteriole leaving; the proximal convoluted tubule coiling in the cortex; the loop of Henle dipping into the medulla with descending and ascending limbs; the distal convoluted tubule back in the cortex; and the collecting duct running down into the medulla towards the pelvis. A network of capillaries surrounds the tubules and joins into a blue branch of the renal vein.
B6b-02-bone-structure-osteon

Two diagrams side by side. Left: a long bone (femur) cut lengthwise, showing the shaft (diaphysis) of thick compact bone around a marrow cavity with yellow marrow, the two enlarged ends (epiphyses) of spongy bone with red marrow, the growth plates, the articular cartilage covering each end, the periosteum on the outside, and a blood vessel entering the bone. Right: an enlarged transverse section of compact bone showing several Haversian systems, each with a central Haversian canal containing a blood vessel, concentric lamellae, osteocytes in lacunae and fine canaliculi radiating out.
B6b-10-synovial-joint-cross-section

Longitudinal section through a typical synovial joint (e.g. the knee, simplified), showing the ends of two bones covered with smooth blue articular cartilage, the joint cavity filled with pale yellow synovial fluid, the synovial membrane lining the inside of the capsule, the fibrous joint capsule, ligaments on the outside joining bone to bone, and a muscle with its tendon attached to one bone.
B7a-01-paramecium-binary-fission-stages

Step-by-step diagram of transverse binary fission in Paramecium in five stages from left to right: (1) a full-grown slipper-shaped Paramecium with cilia, an oral groove, a large bean-shaped macronucleus, a small round micronucleus beside it and two star-shaped contractile vacuoles; (2) the micronucleus dividing into two and the macronucleus elongating; (3) a constriction forming across the middle of the cell, with each half receiving a micronucleus and half of the macronucleus; (4) the constriction deepening; (5) two small daughter Paramecia separating.
B7b-11-double-fertilisation-angiosperms

Diagram of a carpel in longitudinal section showing double fertilisation. Show pollen grains on the stigma, one of which has grown a long pollen tube down through the style into the ovary and through the micropyle of an ovule. Inside the tube near its tip: a tube nucleus and two male nuclei. Inside the ovule's embryo sac: the egg cell with two synergids at the micropyle end, two polar nuclei in the centre and three antipodal cells at the far end. Use two dotted arrows: one from a male nucleus to the egg cell and one from the other male nucleus to the polar nuclei.
B9c-10-coleoptile-phototropism-experiments

A row of seven simple coleoptile experiment drawings, each showing a small pale-green coleoptile growing from a little pot of soil, with yellow light arrows coming from the right-hand side in experiments 1 to 6 and no light (darkness shown by a grey background panel) in experiment 7. 1: intact coleoptile bending towards the light. 2: coleoptile with its tip removed, standing straight and short. 3: coleoptile with a black opaque cap on its tip, standing straight. 4: coleoptile with a black opaque sleeve around the part below the tip, bending towards the light. 5: tip removed and replaced on a thin pale-yellow agar block, bending towards the light. 6: a thin grey mica sheet inserted into the shaded left side just below the tip, standing straight. 7: decapitated coleoptile in darkness with a small agar block placed on its left side only, bending to the right.
